component.name: sparq
component.description: sparq — SOTA Rust RDF + SPARQL engine. This is the checked-in VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) source of truth; the release workflow stamps the released version into a per-release copy attached to the GitHub Release alongside the CycloneDX SBOM.

_comment: [OPUS-4.8] sq-toze.3 (GX-2): VEX justifying the advisories that cargo-deny is configured
to ignore in deny.toml. KEEP THIS IN SYNC WITH deny.toml [advisories].ignore — each entry
here corresponds 1:1 to an ignore there, with the same justification. The entry is an `unmaintained`
informational advisory on a TRANSITIVE dep with no available code-execution / vulnerability
vector and no safe upgrade today; the VEX `analysis.state` is `not_affected` because an
unmaintained-crate notice is not an exploitable weakness in sparq's product. Re-audit when an
upgrade path appears (drop the deny.toml ignore AND the matching entry here). The CycloneDX
`vulnerabilities[].analysis.justification` values are from the CycloneDX impact-analysis

vulnerabilities.description: The `rustls-pemfile` crate is archived; its functionality has been folded into `rustls-pki-types`. This is an `unmaintained` informational advisory, not a vulnerability — no known CVE, CVSS, or exploit.
vulnerabilities.detail: Pulled in transitively via ureq -> rustls-native-certs -> rustls-pemfile. Per the advisory, no safe upgrade is available without an upstream ureq / rustls-native-certs bump; tracked in bead sq-g2xs.

analysis.detail: `rustls-pemfile` parses PEM at TLS-client startup; the archived status carries no known vulnerability and there is no available upgrade. not_affected; re-audit when the upstream ureq/rustls-native-certs path moves to rustls-pki-types. Mirrors the deny.toml [advisories].ignore entry (same reason).
